sanskrit: na caivopayikī bhāryā mānuṣī kṛpaṇā tava vivaśāṃ dharṣayitvā ca kāṃ tvaṃ prītim avāpsyasi
english: A human wife is not suitable for you, nor is she your wretched possession. Having violated a helpless woman against her will, what pleasure will you gain?

sanskrit: prajāpatisamo vipro brahmayoniḥ pitā tava na ca pālayase dharmaṃ lokapālasamaḥ katham
english: Your father is a brahmin equal to Prajāpati, born of Brahmā himself — and you, who are compared to a guardian of the worlds, how is it that you do not uphold dharma?

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ rājarājānaṃ maheśvarasakhaṃ prabhum dhaneśvaraṃ vyapadiśan kathaṃ tv iha na lajjase
english: Citing your brother — the king of kings, the friend of Maheśvara, lord and master of wealth — how is it that you feel no shame here?

sanskrit: ity uktvā prārudat sītā kampayantī payodharau śirodharāṃ ca tanvaṅgī mukhaṃ pracchādya vāsasā
english: Having spoken thus, Sītā wept, her breasts trembling and her slender neck quivering, as she covered her face with the edge of her garment.

sanskrit: tasyā rudatyā bhāminyā dīrghā veṇī susaṃyatā dadṛśe svasitā snigdhā kālī vyālīva mūrdhani
english: As that passionate woman wept, her long, neatly bound braid — dark, lustrous, and black — was seen resting on her head like a serpent.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rāvaṇo vākyaṃ sītayoktaṃ suniṣṭhuram pratyākhyāto 'pi durmedhāḥ punar evābravīd vacaḥ
english: Having heard those harsh words spoken by Sītā, Rāvaṇa, evil-minded though he had been rejected, spoke once more.

sanskrit: kāmam aṅgāni me sīte dunotu makaradhvajaḥ na tvām akāmāṃ suśroṇīṃ sameṣye cāruhāsinīm
english: "Let the god whose banner bears the sea-monster torment my limbs, O Sītā — I will not approach you, fair-hipped and lovely-smiling one, when you are unwilling."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ yat tvam adyāpi mānuṣam āhārabhūtam asmākaṃ rāmam evānurudhyase
english: "What indeed can I do, when even now you keep pining for Rāma — that human who is fit only to be food for us?"

sanskrit: ity uktvā tām anindyāṅgīṃ sa rākṣasagaṇeśvaraḥ tatraivāntarhito bhūtvā jagāmābhimatāṃ diśam
english: Having said this to the blameless-limbed Sītā, that lord of the host of rākṣasas vanished on the spot and departed in his desired direction.

sanskrit: rākṣasībhiḥ parivṛtā vaidehī śokakarśitā sevyamānā trijaṭayā tatraiva nyavasat tadā
english: The princess of Videha, emaciated by grief, surrounded by rākṣasī women and attended upon by Trijaṭā, remained there at that very place.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca rāghavas tu sasaumitriḥ sugrīveṇābhipālitaḥ vasan mālyavataḥ pṛṣṭhe dadarśa vimalaṃ nabhaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Rāghava, together with Saumitri, under Sugrīva's protection, dwelling on the summit of Mount Mālyavat, beheld the clear sky.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā vimale vyomni nirmalaṃ śaśalakṣaṇam grahanakṣatratārābhir anuyātam amitrahā
english: He, the destroyer of enemies, seeing in the clear sky the spotless moon — its hare-mark distinct — attended by planets, asterisms, and stars,

sanskrit: kumudotpalapadmānāṃ gandham ādāya vāyunā mahīdharasthaḥ śītena sahasā pratibodhitaḥ
english: was suddenly roused from sleep by the cool wind as it carried the fragrance of kumuda, utpala, and lotus flowers, while he stood on the mountain.

sanskrit: prabhāte lakṣmaṇaṃ vīram abhyabhāṣata durmanāḥ sītāṃ saṃsmṛtya dharmātmā ruddhāṃ rākṣasaveśmani
english: At daybreak, filled with sorrow, his mind on the righteous path, recalling Sītā imprisoned in the rākṣasa's dwelling, he addressed the heroic Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: gaccha lakṣmaṇa jānīhi kiṣkindhāyāṃ kapīśvaram pramattaṃ grāmyadharmeṣu kṛtaghnaṃ svārthapaṇḍitam
english: "Go, Lakṣmaṇa, and learn of the lord of monkeys in Kiṣkindhā — that ingrate, clever only in his own interests, intoxicated with the pleasures of the senses."

sanskrit: yo 'sau kulādhamo mūḍho mayā rājye 'bhiṣecitaḥ sarvavānaragopucchā yam ṛkṣāś ca bhajanti vai
english: "That lowest of his line, that fool whom I installed on the throne — all the monkeys with their tufted tails and the bears follow him as their lord."

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ nihato vālī mayā raghukulodvaha tvayā saha mahābāho kiṣkindhopavane tadā
english: "O scion of the Raghu line, O mighty-armed one — it was for his sake that Vālin was slain by me alongside you in the forest of Kiṣkindhā."

sanskrit: kṛtaghnaṃ tam ahaṃ manye vānarāpasadaṃ bhuvi yo mām evaṃgato mūḍho na jānīte 'dya lakṣmaṇa
english: "I consider him an ungrateful wretch, the vilest of monkeys on earth — that fool, in such a state as he is, does not even acknowledge me today, Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: asau manye na jānīte samayapratipādanam kṛtopakāraṃ māṃ nūnam avamanyālpayā dhiyā
english: "I think he does not know the fulfilment of his sworn agreement; with his limited intellect, he surely disregards me, who rendered him such service."

sanskrit: yadi tāvad anudyuktaḥ śete kāmasukhātmakaḥ netavyo vālimārgeṇa sarvabhūtagatiṃ tvayā
english: "If he still lies inactive, given over to sensual pleasure, you must send him the way of Vālin — the path that all beings must travel."

sanskrit: athāpi ghaṭate 'smākam arthe vānarapuṃgavaḥ tam ādāyaihi kākutstha tvarāvān bhava mā ciram
english: "Or if that bull among monkeys is still willing to serve our cause, then bring him here, O Kākutstha — make haste and do not delay."

sanskrit: ity ukto lakṣmaṇo bhrātrā guruvākyahite rataḥ pratasthe ruciraṃ gṛhya samārgaṇaguṇaṃ dhanuḥ kiṣkindhādvāram āsādya praviveśānivāritaḥ
english: Thus addressed by his elder brother, Lakṣmaṇa — devoted to the welfare of his guru's words — set forth, taking up his splendid bow strung with a straight bowstring, and reaching the gate of Kiṣkindhā entered it unchallenged.

sanskrit: sakrodha iti taṃ matvā rājā pratyudyayau hariḥ taṃ sadāro vinītātmā sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ pūjayā pratijagrāha prīyamāṇas tadarhayā
english: Perceiving him to be angry, the monkey king Sugrīva, lord of the leaping hosts, went forward to meet him; that self-composed lord of monkeys, together with his wife, received him with joyful honor befitting Lakṣmaṇa's worth.

sanskrit: tam abravīd rāmavacaḥ saumitrir akutobhayaḥ sa tat sarvam aśeṣeṇa śrutvā prahvaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Saumitri, who feared nothing, conveyed Rāma's words to him; having heard it all completely, Sugrīva bowed with joined palms.

sanskrit: sabhṛtyadāro rājendra sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ idam āha vacaḥ prīto lakṣmaṇaṃ narakuñjaram
english: Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, O king of kings, together with his retinue and wives, pleased, spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, that elephant among men.

sanskrit: nāsmi lakṣmaṇa durmedhā na kṛtaghno na nirghṛṇaḥ śrūyatāṃ yaḥ prayatno me sītāparyeṣaṇe kṛtaḥ
english: "I am not evil-minded, Lakṣmaṇa, nor ungrateful, nor merciless — hear what effort I have made in the search for Sītā."

sanskrit: diśaḥ prasthāpitāḥ sarve vinītā harayo mayā sarveṣāṃ ca kṛtaḥ kālo māsenāgamanaṃ punaḥ
english: "All the trained monkeys have been dispatched in every direction by me, and for all of them the time for return was set at one month."

sanskrit: yair iyaṃ savanā sādriḥ sapurā sāgarāmbarā vicetavyā mahī vīra sagrāmanagarākarā
english: "By them this earth, with its forests, mountains, and cities, girdled by the ocean, with its villages, towns, and mines — all of it was to be searched, O hero."

sanskrit: sa māsaḥ pañcarātreṇa pūrṇo bhavitum arhati tataḥ śroṣyasi rāmeṇa sahitaḥ sumahat priyam
english: "That month is due to be completed in five more nights — then, together with Rāma, you will hear exceedingly good tidings."

sanskrit: ity ukto lakṣmaṇas tena vānarendreṇa dhīmatā tyaktvā roṣam adīnātmā sugrīvaṃ pratyapūjayat
english: Thus addressed by that wise lord of monkeys, Lakṣmaṇa — noble-souled and undejected — set aside his anger and honored Sugrīva in return.

sanskrit: sa rāmaṃ sahasugrīvo mālyavatpṛṣṭham āsthitam abhigamyodayaṃ tasya kāryasya pratyavedayat
english: Then Sugrīva, approaching Rāma who was stationed on the summit of Mālyavat, reported to him the progress of that undertaking.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vānarendrās te samājagmuḥ sahasraśaḥ diśas tisro vicityātha na tu ye dakṣiṇāṃ gatāḥ
english: Thus those monkey chiefs came back in thousands, having searched three directions — but not those who had gone south.

sanskrit: ācakhyus te tu rāmāya mahīṃ sāgaramekhalām vicitāṃ na tu vaidehyā darśanaṃ rāvaṇasya vā
english: They reported to Rāma that the earth girdled by the ocean had been searched, but that neither Vaidehī nor Rāvaṇa had been seen.

sanskrit: gatās tu dakṣiṇām āśāṃ ye vai vānarapuṃgavāḥ āśāvāṃs teṣu kākutsthaḥ prāṇān ārto 'py adhārayat
english: But as for the bulls among monkeys who had gone toward the southern quarter, Kākutstha, though tormented, held on to his life placing his hope in them.

sanskrit: dvimāsoparame kāle vyatīte plavagās tataḥ sugrīvam abhigamyedaṃ tvaritā vākyam abruvan
english: When nearly two months had elapsed, those leaping ones then hastily approached Sugrīva and spoke these words.

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ vālinā yat tat sphītaṃ madhuvanaṃ mahat tvayā ca plavagaśreṣṭha tad bhuṅkte pavanātmajaḥ
english: "That great and flourishing Madhu-forest which was guarded by Vālin and then by you, O best of leaping ones — the son of the wind god is now enjoying it."

sanskrit: vāliputro 'ṅgadaś caiva ye cānye plavagarṣabhāḥ vicetuṃ dakṣiṇām āśāṃ rājan prasthāpitās tvayā
english: "Vālin's son Aṅgada and the other bulls among monkeys whom you, O king, dispatched to search the southern quarter —"

sanskrit: teṣāṃ taṃ praṇayaṃ śrutvā mene sa kṛtakṛtyatām kṛtārthānāṃ hi bhṛtyānām etad bhavati ceṣṭitam
english: Hearing that affectionate request of theirs, he concluded that their mission was accomplished — for such is indeed the conduct of servants who have fulfilled their purpose.

sanskrit: sa tad rāmāya medhāvī śaśaṃsa plavagarṣabhaḥ rāmaś cāpy anumānena mene dṛṣṭāṃ tu maithilīm
english: That wise bull among monkeys reported it to Rāma, and Rāma too by inference concluded that the Maithilī princess had indeed been seen.

sanskrit: hanūmatpramukhāś cāpi viśrāntās te plavaṃgamāḥ abhijagmur harīndraṃ taṃ rāmalakṣmaṇasaṃnidhau
english: Those leaping ones, with Hanūmān at their head, having rested, came to that lord of monkeys in the presence of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: gatiṃ ca mukhavarṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā rāmo hanūmataḥ agamat pratyayaṃ bhūyo dṛṣṭā sīteti bhārata
english: Seeing Hanūmān's gait and the color of his face, Rāma became all the more convinced, O Bhārata, that Sītā had been found.

sanskrit: hanūmatpramukhās te tu vānarāḥ pūrṇamānasāḥ praṇemur vidhivad rāmaṃ sugrīvaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tathā
english: Those monkeys, with Hanūmān foremost, their hearts full, bowed down in due form before Rāma, Sugrīva, and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tān uvācāgatān rāmaḥ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ api māṃ jīvayiṣyadhvam api vaḥ kṛtakṛtyatā
english: Taking up his arrow-fitted bow, Rāma spoke to them as they arrived: "Will you restore me to life? Have you accomplished your purpose?"

sanskrit: api rājyam ayodhyāyāṃ kārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ nihatya samare śatrūn āhṛtya janakātmajām
english: "Shall I once again rule the kingdom in Ayodhyā, having slain my enemies in battle and recovered the daughter of Janaka?"

sanskrit: amokṣayitvā vaidehīm ahatvā ca ripūn raṇe hṛtadāro 'vadhūtaś ca nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "Without freeing Vaidehī and without slaying my foes in battle, robbed of my wife and cast aside, I have no will to live."

sanskrit: ity uktavacanaṃ rāmaṃ pratyuvācānilātmajaḥ priyam ākhyāmi te rāma dṛṣṭā sā jānakī mayā
english: To Rāma who had spoken thus, the son of the wind god replied: "I bring you glad tidings, Rāma — I have seen that Jānakī."

sanskrit: vicitya dakṣiṇām āśāṃ saparvatavanākarām śrāntāḥ kāle vyatīte sma dṛṣṭavanto mahāguhām
english: "Having searched the southern quarter with its mountains, forests, and mines, we grew weary as time passed and came upon a great cave."

sanskrit: praviśāmo vayaṃ tāṃ tu bahuyojanam āyatām andhakārāṃ suvipināṃ gahanāṃ kīṭasevitām
english: "We entered it — extending for many leagues, dark, thickly forested, impenetrable, teeming with insects."

sanskrit: gatvā sumahad adhvānam ādityasya prabhāṃ tataḥ dṛṣṭavantaḥ sma tatraiva bhavanaṃ divyam antarā
english: "After traveling a very great distance, we then saw the light of the sun and right there in the midst of it a divine dwelling."

sanskrit: mayasya kila daityasya tadāsīd veśma rāghava tatra prabhāvatī nāma tapo 'tapyata tāpasī
english: "It was said to have been the abode of the Daitya Maya, O Rāghava; there an ascetic woman named Prabhāvatī performed her austerities."

sanskrit: tayā dattāni bhojyāni pānāni vividhāni ca bhuktvā labdhabalāḥ santas tayoktena pathā tataḥ
english: "Having eaten the food and various drinks given by her, we regained our strength and then went along the path she had shown us."

sanskrit: niryāya tasmād uddeśāt paśyāmo lavaṇāmbhasaḥ samīpe sahyamalayau darduraṃ ca mahāgirim
english: "Emerging from that place, we saw near the salt-watered sea the Sahya and Malaya ranges and the great mountain Dardura."

sanskrit: tato malayam āruhya paśyanto varuṇālayam viṣaṇṇā vyathitāḥ khinnā nirāśā jīvite bhṛśam
english: "Then, having climbed Malaya and gazing at Varuṇa's ocean, we sat dejected, distressed, despondent, wholly bereft of hope for life."

sanskrit: anekaśatavistīrṇaṃ yojanānāṃ mahodadhim timinakrajhaṣāvāsaṃ cintayantaḥ suduḥkhitāḥ
english: "Contemplating the great ocean stretching hundreds of leagues in width, the home of timinakra fish and other great sea creatures, we were exceedingly sorrowful."

sanskrit: tatrānaśanasaṃkalpaṃ kṛtvāsīnā vayaṃ tadā tataḥ kathānte gṛdhrasya jaṭāyor abhavat kathā
english: "Having resolved to fast unto death, we sat there; then, at the end of our talk, the subject of the vulture Jaṭāyu came up."

sanskrit: tataḥ parvataśṛṅgābhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayāvaham pakṣiṇaṃ dṛṣṭavantaḥ sma vainateyam ivāparam
english: "Then we saw a bird — terrible in form, terrifying, like another Vainateya — its shape resembling a mountain peak."

sanskrit: so 'smān atarkayad bhoktum athābhyetya vaco 'bravīt bhoḥ ka eṣa mama bhrātur jaṭāyoḥ kurute kathām
english: "He had intended to eat us, but then he came up and spoke: 'Ho, who is this who speaks of my brother Jaṭāyu?'"

sanskrit: saṃpātir nāma tasyāhaṃ jyeṣṭho bhrātā khagādhipaḥ anyonyaspardhayārūḍhāv āvām ādityasaṃsadam
english: "'I am Saṃpāti by name, the elder brother of Jaṭāyu, lord of birds; the two of us, competing with each other, had soared to the assembly of the Sun.'"

sanskrit: tato dagdhāv imau pakṣau na dagdhau tu jaṭāyuṣaḥ tadā me ciradṛṣṭaḥ sa bhrātā gṛdhrapatiḥ priyaḥ nirdagdhapakṣaḥ patito hy aham asmin mahāgirau
english: "'Then my wings were burned, but Jaṭāyu's wings were not; at that time, that beloved brother of mine, king of vultures, whom I had not seen for long — and I, my wings utterly scorched, fell onto this great mountain.'"

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ vadato 'smābhir hato bhrātā niveditaḥ vyasanaṃ bhavataś cedaṃ saṃkṣepād vai niveditam
english: "As he spoke thus, we reported to him that his brother had been slain; we also briefly informed him of your misfortune."

sanskrit: sa saṃpātis tadā rājañ śrutvā sumahad apriyam viṣaṇṇacetāḥ papraccha punar asmān ariṃdama
english: "Then Saṃpāti, O king, O subduer of foes, having heard that most grievous news, his heart overwhelmed, questioned us further."

sanskrit: kaḥ sa rāmaḥ kathaṃ sītā jaṭāyuś ca kathaṃ hataḥ icchāmi sarvam evaitac chrotuṃ plavagasattamāḥ
english: "'Who is this Rāma? What has become of Sītā? And how was Jaṭāyu slain? O best of leaping ones, I wish to hear all of this.'"

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ sarvam evaitaṃ bhavato vyasanāgamam prāyopaveśane caiva hetuṃ vistarato 'bruvam
english: "I then described to him at length the entire story of your calamity and also the reason for our resolve to fast unto death."

sanskrit: so 'smān utthāpayām āsa vākyenānena pakṣirāṭ rāvaṇo vidito mahyaṃ laṅkā cāsya mahāpurī
english: "That king of birds then raised us up with these words: 'Rāvaṇa is known to me, and so is his great city of Laṅkā.'"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā pāre samudrasya trikūṭagirikandare bhavitrī tatra vaidehī na me 'sty atra vicāraṇā
english: "'Vaidehī will be found on the far side of the ocean, in the cave of Mount Trikūṭa — of this I have no doubt.'"

sanskrit: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā vayam utthāya satvarāḥ sāgaraplavane mantraṃ mantrayāmaḥ paraṃtapa
english: "Hearing his words, we arose quickly and took counsel together about crossing the ocean, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: nādhyavasyad yadā kaś cit sāgarasya vilaṅghane tataḥ pitaram āviśya pupluve 'haṃ mahārṇavam śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ nihatya jalarākṣasīm
english: "When no one else resolved to cross the ocean, I then, entering into my father's spirit, leaped across the great sea — a hundred leagues in width — slaying a water-rākṣasī."

sanskrit: tatra sītā mayā dṛṣṭā rāvaṇāntaḥpure satī upavāsatapaḥśīlā bhartṛdarśanalālasā jaṭilā maladigdhāṅgī kṛśā dīnā tapasvinī
english: "There Sītā was seen by me, a chaste woman in Rāvaṇa's inner apartments — devoted to fasting and austerity, longing to see her husband, her hair matted, her body smeared with grime, emaciated, wretched, an ascetic."

sanskrit: nimittais tām ahaṃ sītām upalabhya pṛthagvidhaiḥ upasṛtyābruvaṃ cāryām abhigamya rahogatām
english: "Having identified that Sītā by various signs, I approached her as she was alone in a secluded spot and addressed that noble lady."

sanskrit: sīte rāmasya dūto 'haṃ vānaro mārutātmajaḥ tvaddarśanam abhiprepsur iha prāpto vihāyasā
english: "'Sītā, I am a monkey, the son of Mārutha, Rāma's messenger — I have come here through the sky, eager to see you.'"

sanskrit: rājaputrau kuśalinau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau sarvaśākhāmṛgendreṇa sugrīveṇābhipālitau
english: "'The two princes, brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are well, and are under the protection of Sugrīva, lord of all the tree-dwelling monkeys.'"

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ tvābravīd rāmaḥ sīte saumitriṇā saha sakhibhāvāc ca sugrīvaḥ kuśalaṃ tvānupṛcchati
english: "'Rāma enquires after your well-being, Sītā, together with Saumitri; and Sugrīva, in friendship, likewise enquires after your welfare.'"

sanskrit: kṣipram eṣyati te bhartā sarvaśākhāmṛgaiḥ saha pratyayaṃ kuru me devi vānaro 'smi na rākṣasaḥ
english: "'Your husband will come swiftly with all the monkeys; trust me, O queen — I am a monkey, not a rākṣasa.'"

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva ca dhyātvā sītā māṃ pratyuvāca ha avaimi tvāṃ hanūmantam avindhyavacanād aham
english: "After reflecting for a moment, Sītā spoke to me: 'I know you to be Hanūmān by the words of Avindhya.'"

sanskrit: avindhyo hi mahābāho rākṣaso vṛddhasaṃmataḥ kathitas tena sugrīvas tvadvidhaiḥ sacivair vṛtaḥ
english: "'For Avindhya, O mighty-armed one, is a rākṣasa respected by the elders; by him Sugrīva was described as attended by ministers such as you.'"

sanskrit: gamyatām iti coktvā māṃ sītā prādād imaṃ maṇim dhāritā yena vaidehī kālam etam aninditā
english: "Saying 'You may go,' Sītā gave me this jewel — the one with which the blameless Vaidehī has borne this time of trial."

sanskrit: pratyayārthaṃ kathāṃ cemāṃ kathayām āsa jānakī kṣiptām iṣīkāṃ kākasya citrakūṭe mahāgirau bhavatā puruṣavyāghra pratyabhijñānakāraṇāt
english: "For the sake of proof, Jānakī also told this tale: the blade of grass hurled at the crow on the great mountain Citrakūṭa by you, O tiger among men, as a token of recognition."

sanskrit: śrāvayitvā tadātmānaṃ tato dagdhvā ca tāṃ purīm saṃprāpta iti taṃ rāmaḥ priyavādinam arcayat
english: "Having made him hear it himself, and then having burned that city, I have returned" — so spoke he; and Rāma honored that bearer of glad tidings.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tatas tatraiva rāmasya samāsīnasya taiḥ saha samājagmuḥ kapiśreṣṭhāḥ sugrīvavacanāt tadā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, right there where Rāma was seated among them, the foremost of monkeys came together at that time, acting on Sugrīva's command.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām śvaśuro vālinaḥ śrīmān suṣeṇo rāmam abhyayāt
english: Attended by a thousand crores of swift monkeys, the glorious Suṣeṇa — father-in-law of Vālin — approached Rāma.
